stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: A new low for American workers
stories.text: Workers in the United States are earning a historically low share of the value they produce, according to new data released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). The BLS estimates that the labor share of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) “was 52.8 percent in the second quarter of 2026.” This is the lowest level that the BLS has seen since it first began recording labor share in 1947. Labor share has been on a downward trend for months. In the first quarter of 2026, labor share was 53.7%, which was, at the time, a historic low. Over the last 25 years, the labor share of income has plummeted. In the first quarter of 2000, the labor share was 63.9% . But while labor’s share of GDP is collapsing, U.S. corporate profits are surging. In the second quarter of 2026, corporate profits increased 9% compared to the first quarter of the year, according to data released in August by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Corporate profits “ increased $400.9 billion in the second quarter, compared with an increase of $74.4 billion in the first quarter ,” according to the BEA. stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: How Status Quo Democrats Could Create Another Trump
stories.text: When I look back on all of my work over the last 30 years, one of the projects I’m most proud of is Meltdown , an audio series I did in 2021 with acclaimed director Alex Gibney that reveals the untold story of how Obama-era Democrats turning promises of economic hope and change into more of the same created the backlash conditions for the rise of Donald Trump. It is a miracle Meltdown ever got made, because calling its tale “untold” is an understatement. The story of Obama’s 2008 victory concluding with Trump’s 2016 win involves a sequence of economic facts and events that have been suppressed, shadowbanned, memory-holed, and censored from America’s political conversation. This is particularly true in media outlets that serve liberals, who seek comfort in the idea that Trump is an anomaly rather than a symptom of something their own political party participated in creating. Every now and again, there are attempts to warn about this perpetual doom loop. stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: Newsom Killed The AI Kill Switch
stories.text: Amid mounting warnings that artificial intelligence could lead to the end of humanity, California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D), a leading 2028 presidential hopeful, has been pushing new, but limited , AI safeguards as he adopts a more populist stance on the emerging technology. What he’d likely prefer to downplay is his veto of a bill designed to guard against the AI apocalypse — at the urging of California-based Big Tech companies whose employees now say doomsday could be closer than ever. Two years ago, Newsom vetoed a California bill, Senate Bill 1047 , that would have held AI firms liable for damages unleashed on society and required a “kill switch” for AI systems that went rogue. While the bill was framed as a potential model for the rest of the country, Newsom said his veto aimed to protect the public “against actual threats without unnecessarily thwarting the promise of this technology to advance the public good.” Insiders now say AI’s threats are more pronounced than ever. stories.title: Israeli Strike in Lebanon Kills 12 People From a Single Family, Including 6 Children
stories.text: A local sheikh gives a final prayer over the body of one of six children killed in a September 7, 2026 Israeli airstrike on the Farhat family home in Kfar Remman, in Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon that killed a total of 12 members of the family. KFAR REMMAN, Lebanon—“They are killing children. That’s what they’re doing,” Baker Malak said, pointing to the tiny coffins being carried through the streets of the town of Kfar Remman in southern Lebanon on Tuesday. He walked alongside hundreds of mourners in a funeral procession to bury 12 members of a single family, half of them children, killed in an Israeli airstrike on their home a day earlier. Nearby, mourners carried the coffin of 18-year-old paramedic Ali Shahrour, killed in a separate strike on the town the same day. The procession wound through streets scarred by months of bombardment as an Israeli drone buzzed incessantly overhead. “When Israel sees that the Lebanese government is doing nothing, they will keep targeting children,” said Malak.
